queries: The Santa Teresa lemon (Citrus limon) has been evaluated in field trials and controlled inoculation studies for its resistance to mal secco disease, caused by the fungal pathogen Phoma tracheiphila. Among the various lemon clones and cultivars screened for susceptibility, Santa Teresa consistently demonstrated the highest level of tolerance, exhibiting markedly reduced symptom development, slower disease progression, and lower rates of vascular discoloration compared to other commercial clones such as Femminello, Eureka, and Lisbon. This resistance is attributed to a combination of anatomical barriers, including thicker cuticle and more compact xylem vessels, as well as biochemical responses involving the accumulation of phenolic compounds and phytoalexins. In multi-year trials conducted in regions with high disease pressure, Santa Teresa maintained significantly lower infection indices and showed superior recovery and regrowth after pruning of infected branches. Its genetic background, possibly derived from a natural mutation or hybridization event, confers a durable resistance that has not been overcome by local pathogen isolates. Consequently, Santa Teresa is recommended as a rootstock or scion for new plantings in areas where mal secco is endemic, and it serves as a valuable genetic resource for breeding programs aimed at developing resistant lemon varieties. The findings underscore the importance of clonal selection in citrus disease management and highlight Santa Teresa as the most promising candidate for sustainable lemon cultivation in Mediterranean climates.
rerank_query_used: What disease does the Santa Teresa lemon show higher resistance to than any other clone discovered to date, making it considered promising?

candidates.text:
## Description from The Citrus Industry Vol. 1 (1967)  
"This comparatively new Italian selection of the Femminello Ovale type is considered to be highly promising because of its greater resistance to the mal secco disease than any other clone found thus far. The parent tree was an old disease-free tree discovered in a Femminello orchard that had almost been destroyed by the disease (Russo, 1955). It is said to be the variety currently most planted as a replacement in areas of Italy where the disease is severe."
